subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Verifiable Credentials
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Verifiable Credentials.

hook.text: Instead of showing your entire driver's license, what if you could prove just one fact: you can drive.

buildup.text: Verifiable credentials are digital proofs that confirm specific claims without revealing unnecessary data.

discovery.text: Using cryptography, a verifier can confirm the credential is authentic without contacting the issuer.

twist.text: This reverses the current model. Today, verification means sharing your full identity and hoping it's protected.

climax.text: Verifiable credentials promise a future where proving something about yourself doesn't mean revealing everything.

punchline.text: Prove the fact. Keep everything else private.

quiz.question: How do verifiable credentials differ from traditional ID verification?
options: They prove specific claims without revealing unnecessary personal data
They require more personal data than traditional methods
They only work for government services
